question.problem:
Which of the following probabilities could be approximated using the normal approximation of the binomial distribution?

I. The probability of getting $10$ ones on $25$ rolls of a biased $6$-sided die if the probability of getting one in a single roll is $0.4.$

II. The probability of a student getting more than $10$ correct answers on a $20$-question test if the student has $60%$ probability of correctly answering each question.

III. The probability that a fair spinner with twenty-five regions, numbered from $1$ through $25,$ lands on seven more than $5$ times out of $100$ spins.
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Let's now examine each situation.

- In situation I, we have $n=25$ and $p=0.4.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =25\cdot 0.4 \\  & =10 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =25\cdot (1-0.4) \\  & =15 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

- In situation II, we have $n=20$ and $p=0.6.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =20\cdot 0.6 \\  & =12 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =20\cdot (1-0.6) \\  & =8 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

- In situation III, we have $n=100$ and $p=\frac{1}{25}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =100\cdot \frac{1}{25} \\  & =4 \\  & ≯5.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
